teacher.key_rationale: The small intestine receives pancreatic juice from the pancreas (✓); the basic pancreatic juice neutralises the acidic partially digested food arriving from the stomach (✓); and digested nutrients pass into blood vessels in the small-intestine wall (✓). Row B is the trap for a student who drops the absorption condition and treats the small intestine as merely a tube passing food onward.
